tasks.short: Hand out the paper intake form and type it into the record, ask about the complaint and history, and write the history note.

steps.what: Patient fills the intake questionnaire in the patient portal before the first visit
Chiropractor hands out the paper intake form and types it into the record
Chiropractor asks the patient's consent to record the consultation and notes the answer
Chiropractor obtains patients' medical histories in conversation
Chiropractor records the medical history note

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the patient's consent, and the intake answers.
loop.output: A draft history note in the record's structure.
loop.check: A validator flags any medication, diagnosis or red-flag symptom not in the transcript or intake. The chiropractor reads the whole draft against what the patient said: nothing added, nothing important left out, negations right; unclear passages are written by hand before saving.
loop.stop: One draft per consultation; if the patient declines recording or the draft is rejected, the chiropractor writes the note.
loop.why_not_simpler: Patients tell their history in their own words; a form does not capture it.

tasks.design: New patients fill the intake questionnaire in the practice's patient portal before the first visit, and the answers fill structured fields in the record ({OTHER}), so the paper form is not typed in. With consent, a scribe drafts the history note from the consultation; a validator flags medication, diagnoses or red-flag symptoms not in the transcript or intake, and the chiropractor validates before saving. The conversation stays with the chiropractor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Intake forms were typed in and history notes written after the visit.
tasks.enabler_now: Scribes draft notes the clinician validates; portals take intake questionnaires.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts can add statements no one made.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing the red-flag symptom that changes everything.
tasks.altitude: The chiropractor validates drafts instead of typing.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber records the consultation and the clinician validates before the note goes into the record.
At Capio Ramsay Santé, 1,295 clinicians reported time per note falling from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes with Tandem notes; three of seven authors were from the vendor.
Providers are legally responsible for careful use of generative AI.

assumptions: Boundary: from the new patient to the history recorded; examination is outside.
Input contract: patient consent for recording; fallback is typing.
Patients fill the intake before the visit in about the time the paper form took; a little patient time is priced.

Asking consent to record is shown as its own step (s1b) and is not counted again as new work. s3 keeps 50: about 80% of patients agree to recording; for the rest the note is typed as today, and every draft is read in full.
research_questions: How often does the validator flag a statement?

incremental.description: Patients fill the intake questionnaire online.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many patients decline recording and fill the paper form (s1 60, s3 80) (14.1); high: most intakes online and recorded (31.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review the history and earlier records, question and examine the patient, interpret x-rays, and record the diagnosis.

steps.what: Chiropractor reviews patients' health and medical histories across several screens
Chiropractor questions, observes and examines patients
Chiropractor interprets x-rays to diagnose health problems
Chiropractor records the diagnosis: as free text today; from a coded pick list with a short note after the change

tasks.design: A visit summary in the record ({OTHER}) shows complaints, earlier findings, imaging reports and red flags together, so the chiropractor does not open several screens. The diagnosis is recorded from a coded pick list with a short note; recording it keeps its time. Questioning, examining and interpreting x-rays stay with the chiropractor; no software proposes diagnoses.
tasks.previous_blocker: History sat in several screens and diagnoses were written in free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice records show visit summaries and coded diagnosis lists.
tasks.still_hard: Imaging reports from other providers arrive as PDFs.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling what the x-ray does not show.

evidence.claim: Practice records can show visit summaries and coded diagnosis pick lists.
Decision software is usually MDR class IIa or higher; here no software proposes diagnoses.

assumptions: Boundary: from the history recorded to the diagnosis recorded; treatment is outside.
Input contract: records hold earlier findings; fallback is opening each screen.
Diagnosing and recording the diagnosis stay with the chiropractor and keep their full time; the diagnosis is a first record.

incremental.description: No new work: a note when no code fits is part of recording the diagnosis in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly new patients with little history (s1 90) (1.5); high: returning patients with long records (6.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write treatment notes after each visit, update the treatment plan and progress measures, file incoming letters and reports, and check the record before closing the episode.

steps.what: Chiropractor asks the patient's consent to record the visit and notes the answer
Chiropractor writes treatment notes to maintain accurate case histories

loop.input: The recorded treatment visit, with the patient's consent.
loop.output: A draft treatment note in the record's structure.
loop.check: A validator flags any technique, region or finding not in the transcript. The chiropractor reads the whole draft against the visit: nothing added, nothing missed, findings and regions right; unclear passages are written by hand before saving.
loop.stop: One draft per visit; if the patient declines recording or the draft is rejected, the chiropractor writes the note.
loop.why_not_simpler: Visits differ; a template note gets copied without change.

steps.what: Patient fills the short progress questionnaire in the portal before the visit
Chiropractor updates the treatment plan and progress measures
Chiropractor files incoming letters and imaging reports in the case history
Chiropractor checks the case history is complete before closing the episode

tasks.design: With consent, a scribe drafts the treatment note from the visit; a validator flags techniques, regions or findings not in the transcript, and the chiropractor validates before saving. Patients fill short progress questionnaires (pain, function) in the portal before each visit, and the record ({OTHER}) plots them, so progress is not measured and charted by hand. Letters and imaging reports arrive through secure messaging and attach to the case history without scanning. Checking the record before closing stays with the chiropractor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were typed after visits, progress charted by hand and paper reports scanned and filed.
tasks.enabler_now: Scribes draft notes; portals collect progress questionnaires; secure messaging attaches reports.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts can add techniques that were not used.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing in the history why a patient keeps relapsing.
tasks.altitude: The chiropractor validates drafts instead of typing.

reach.learn: Whether progress is visible to them.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber records the consultation and the clinician validates before the note goes into the record.
The dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.
Ambient recording captures staff performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the visit done to the episode closed; billing is outside.
Input contract: patient consent for recording; fallback is typing.
Patients fill progress questionnaires before visits; a little patient time is priced.
Asking consent to record is its own step (s0) and is not counted again as new work. s3 keeps 10 for letters that still come by post.
research_questions: How long does editing drafted notes take?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many patients decline recording and half of reports still come by post (s1 80, s3 50) (29.2); high: most visits recorded and reports received electronically (51.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Decide a referral is needed and discuss it with the patient, write the referral letter, check it, send it, and call the practitioner for urgent cases.

steps.what: Chiropractor decides to refer patients to appropriate health practitioners and discusses it
Chiropractor writes the referral letter

loop.input: The record: history, findings, diagnosis and treatment so far.
loop.output: A draft referral letter with the question for the other practitioner.
loop.check: A validator flags any finding or medication not in the record. The chiropractor reads each finding in the letter against the record (it says what was found, nothing overstated) and edits every letter.
loop.stop: One draft per referral; if rejected, the chiropractor writes the letter.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each referral needs its own question and story; a template gives only the frame.

steps.what: Chiropractor checks the final referral letter
Chiropractor sends the referral letter: by post or e-mail today, by one release through secure messaging after the change
Chiropractor consults with the other practitioner by phone for urgent cases

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts the referral letter from the record ({OTHER}); a validator flags findings or medication not in the record, and the chiropractor edits every letter. The chiropractor checks the final letter and sends it once to the other practitioner through secure messaging instead of post or e-mail. Deciding to refer, discussing it and calling about urgent cases stay with the chiropractor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Letters were written from scratch and sent by post or e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Clinical tools draft referral letters from the record; secure messaging is standard.
tasks.still_hard: Some practitioners do not take secure messages.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting the case that must go to a doctor today.
tasks.altitude: The chiropractor edits letters instead of writing them.

reach.learn: Whether letters state a clear question.

evidence.claim: Juvoly drafts referral letters and suggests ICPC, ICD-10 and SNOMED codes.
Providers are legally responsible for careful use of generative AI.

assumptions: Boundary: from the diagnosis to the letter sent; the other practitioner's care is outside.
Input contract: secure messaging available; fallback is post.
Receiving practitioners read secure messages as they did letters.
s2 keeps 60: details and history fill from the record, but the chiropractor reads and edits every letter.
research_questions: How much of each drafted letter is kept?

incremental.description: Chiropractor posts letters to practitioners without secure messaging.

approvals.approved_version: The referral letter exactly as checked by the chiropractor in s3, sent once through secure messaging to the named practitioner; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: drafts need heavy edits and many practitioners lack secure messaging (s2 75, s4 60) (9.0); high: most letters go by secure messaging (16.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The chiropractor keeps taking histories, examining, diagnosing and deciding on referrals; typed intake forms, typed notes, hand-charted progress and letters from scratch shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A chiropractor with more time for patients.
